note: Saturday 07:00 SGT weekend run, after the Fri 31 Jul US close and sweeping Sat 1 Aug weekend news (markets shut). Dominant threads: (1) US stocks closed July at RECORDS on a two-day relief rally — Fri 31 Jul S&P +0.7% to 7,489.72, Nasdaq +1.0%, Dow +0.53% — as Amazon's AWS +37% blowout and combined hyperscaler capex guidance of $720-745bn re-validated AI spend; (2) the bond market went the other way — 10Y to 4.73%, a one-year high, on sticky 3.3% core PCE and a hawkish Fed, with ~53-61% odds priced for a September hike; (3) the weekend catalyst: Iran attacked two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 Aug, firming oil (Brent ~$90) and keeping the US-Iran pause broken even as a 10-day ceasefire is discussed; (4) gold held ~$4,080 near a record. 6 of 12 items are dated 31 Jul-1 Aug (last 24-48h). Every item source-verified.

items.headline: Iran attacks two tankers in Strait of Hormuz on 1 Aug; oil firms, US-Iran pause stays broken
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck and disabled two tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz under US military escort on 1 Aug, with the UAE reporting missiles hit two of its tankers in Omani waters, killing one crew member; four other tankers turned back. Oil rose on the news after a week in which prices had fallen more than 5% on de-escalation hopes — WTI settled ~$84.67 and Brent ~$90.12 on Friday. Regional mediators have floated a 10-day ceasefire and Iran-Oman weekend talks were described as constructive, but strikes continue on both sides.
items.actionable: The fresh weekend Hormuz attack re-arms the oil/inflation premium that pressures the rate-sensitive book (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech) while the Fed stays hawkish, but it restores the geopolitical safe-haven bid under gold/silver and lifts the small energy long. Keep gold-heavy GDX as the hedge against the pause staying broken; watch whether the 10-day ceasefire proposal holds when Asia/oil reopen — the Hormuz front is again the key cross-portfolio swing factor.

items.headline: Stocks close July at records: S&P +0.7% to 7,489.72, Nasdaq +1.0%, Dow's 4th straight winning month
items.summary: US equities capped a volatile July at record highs on Friday, extending Thursday's relief rally. The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to a record 7,489.72, the Nasdaq gained 1.0% to 25,373.85 and the Dow added 276.97 points (+0.53%) to 52,485.03 — all three posted weekly gains and the Dow logged a fourth straight winning month. Amazon jumped ~15% on its AWS blowout and the four megacap hyperscalers now guide to a combined $720-745bn of 2026 capital spending, re-validating the AI-infrastructure thesis. The VIX collapsed to 15.99 as equity fear drained.
items.actionable: The AI-capex-doubt scare that had pressured the SMIC/HK-tech chip leg fully reversed — a relief for the tech-beta parts of the book. But the S&P at a fresh record with the 10Y at a one-year-high 4.73% and September a live hike risk leaves little valuation cushion. Don't chase the record; keep the USD cash pile as dry powder and let next week's SGX/HK earnings and the delayed Flow Show confirm the risk-on turn before redeploying.

items.headline: 10Y hits 4.73%, a one-year high; ~53-61% odds priced for a September Fed hike
items.summary: The bond market diverged sharply from the equity rally: the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.73%, its highest in over a year, and the 2-year hit fresh 2026 highs as sticky June core PCE (+3.3% y/y) and Chair Warsh's hawkish-hold framing kept higher-for-longer intact. Rate-hike markets now price roughly 53-61% odds of a 25bp September hike (Kalshi ~53%, Polymarket ~52%, CME FedWatch ~60%) after three FOMC dissents favored an immediate hike at the 29 Jul meeting.
items.actionable: The one-year-high 10Y and a coin-flip-plus September hike are the direct higher-for-longer headwind for levered silver and SGX REITs, and a warning for the most rate-sensitive, cyclical parts of the book. Hedge the rate-sensitive sleeve rather than adding leverage into it; the productive USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as dry powder into the September decision.

items.headline: Gold holds ~$4,080 near a record; silver ~$57-59 on the sticky-inflation/haven bid
items.summary: Gold held its ground near $4,070-4,100/oz into month-end — close to a record — as sticky June core PCE (+3.3% y/y), the reignited US-Iran conflict and the one-year-high 10Y drew both a haven and an inflation-hedge bid; spot traded ~$4,066 on 30 Jul and ~$4,102 on 27 Jul. Silver held roughly $57-59/oz. Gold funds took their largest weekly inflow since April, and the structural silver-deficit thesis (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit) remains intact.
items.actionable: The book's core held firm even into a risk-on equity tape and rising real-rate pressure — gold near a record is the cleanest hold and the steadier hedge against the reignited Iran risk and sticky inflation; favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage while the higher-for-longer Fed (10Y 4.73%) keeps real rates a two-sided pull on silver. Hold the core; hedge the silver-vs-gold spread rather than adding leverage into the record.

items.headline: Apple falls ~7% on soft Services and China; the one blemish on a strong megacap earnings gauntlet
items.summary: Apple shares fell ~7% on Friday, the biggest drag on the Dow, as investors flagged underwhelming Services growth and China revenue against otherwise strong fiscal-Q3 hardware numbers (revenue +16.6% y/y, iPhone +22%). The move contrasted with Amazon's ~15% surge on its AWS +37% blowout, leaving Apple as the lone soft spot in a mega-cap earnings run that otherwise powered the two-day rally to records.
items.actionable: Idiosyncratic to Apple (a Services/China miss against a strong iPhone quarter) rather than an AI-capex or macro signal, so limited read-through to the portfolio — the AMZN/MSFT capex re-validation is the more important tech tape for the SMIC chip leg and HK-tech complex. Notable mainly as the one blemish on an otherwise constructive megacap gauntlet.

items.headline: Crypto consolidates over the weekend: Bitcoin ~$62.9k, Ether ~$1,917, sentiment stuck in 'Fear'
items.summary: Crypto traded sideways into the weekend after the late-July correction: Bitcoin hovered around $62,000-65,000 (~$62,865) after rejection near the top of its descending channel, Ether held ~$1,917 and the crypto Fear & Greed index sat in the low-30s ('Fear'). With no crypto-specific catalyst, the complex continues to trade as a risk-appetite barometer off the macro rate channel; thin weekend liquidity leaves it prone to sharper swings.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is the cleanest read on the risk-appetite impulse — its failure to break higher despite the equity records flags that the rate backdrop is capping risk. Treat it as a barometer: a further hawkish repricing into September would pressure both crypto and the metals/REIT rate-sensitivity trade; a dovish data surprise would relieve both. Watch for weekend-liquidity air-pockets around the Hormuz headlines.

items.headline: Amazon jumps ~15% on AWS +37% blowout; four hyperscalers now guide to $720-745B 2026 capex
items.summary: Amazon rose ~15% after a Q2 beat led by AWS, which grew 37% year-over-year to $42.23B — its fastest in 18 quarters and well above the ~31% consensus — with AI and custom-chip units each running above a $25B run-rate; the company raised its 2026 capex plan to ~$220B. Combined with Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta, the four hyperscalers now guide to $720-745B of cumulative 2026 capital spending, directly reversing the AI-overcapacity narrative that had wiped >$1trn from semis the prior week.
items.actionable: The AWS +37% blowout and the $720-745bn hyperscaler capex guide re-validate the AI-infrastructure spend that the semis rout had doubted — a positive read-through to the SMIC chip leg and the whole AI-hardware complex. It argues the internet/platform layer AND the chip layer both benefit when hyperscaler capex re-accelerates; keep Tencent/Xiaomi favored but the acute bear case on the chip leg has eased.

items.headline: Q2 GDP slows to +1.5%, core PCE sticky at +3.3% — 'stagflation-lite' keeps the Fed hawkish
items.summary: The advance Q2 GDP print came in at +1.5% annualized, down from +2.1% in Q1 and below expectations — a clear growth slowdown. June headline PCE rose +3.7% y/y and core PCE stayed sticky at +3.3% y/y (in line, prior 3.4%), well above the 2% target. The combination validated the three July FOMC hike dissents and Chair Warsh's hawkish framing, sending the 10Y toward 4.73% and the 2Y to fresh 2026 highs even as equities rallied to records.
items.actionable: Sticky 3.3% core PCE keeps September a live hike risk — the direct higher-for-longer headwind for levered silver and SGX REITs, with the 10Y at a one-year high. The sub-trend growth read is a warning for the most cyclical, rate-sensitive parts of the book. Keep the big USD cash pile (~3.5-3.75%) as productive dry powder and hedge the rate-sensitive sleeve rather than adding leverage into it.

items.headline: Semis rebound with the tape but Burry adds to his Micron short (24 Jul, at $933.86)
items.summary: Semiconductors bounced alongside the AWS/MSFT-led rally after a >$1trn drawdown since 24 Jul, with SMIC's HK line and the broad SOX recovering. But Michael Burry — now publishing on Substack after deregistering Scion — disclosed adding to his Micron short on 24 Jul at $933.86, part of an expanded NVDA/MU/AMAT/SOXX/TSLA/CAT bear book arguing the SOX sits near the top of its 15-year forward-P/E band and AI-capex can't justify valuations. Tepper (Q1 13F) and Congress's Newhouse remain on the memory-bull side.
items.actionable: The AWS/hyperscaler capex re-validation eases the acute bear case on the SMIC chip leg near-term, but Burry's fresh, larger Micron short is the standing warning that the group is richly valued into any capex wobble. Continue favoring the internet/consumer HK names (Tencent, Xiaomi) as the core while treating the chip leg as higher-beta and two-sided; size for volatility.

items.headline: SGX earnings season opens with STI near a record; banks upgraded to Overweight, DBS reports 6 Aug
items.summary: Singapore shares sit near record territory — the STI printed ~5,561 on 15 Jul (+21% total return YTD) — as earnings season opens: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug, DBS 6 Aug, and OCBC/UOB 7 Aug. SG banks were upgraded to Overweight by several houses on resilient NIMs and capital returns, while the S-REIT sleeve navigates the higher-for-longer rate backdrop; Keppel DC REIT earlier posted 1H26 DPU +11.3%.
items.actionable: A constructive backdrop for the SGX banks/REIT sleeve into next week's prints, but the hawkish Fed (10Y 4.73%) and the oil-spike inflation risk are fresh headwinds for the rate-sensitive S-REITs. Watch DBS results 6 Aug (guided FY26 slightly lower) and CapLand Ascendas REIT 5 Aug; the banks are the more insulated leg vs the REITs into a higher-for-longer path.

items.headline: China rare-earth enforcement tightens; MP/USAR on control list, 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff nears
items.summary: China's rare-earth grip tightened: MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 (a reporting-and-reward enforcement regime) took effect 1 Jul, and export curbs were extended to 14 EU firms on 24 Jul, while MP Materials and USA Rare Earth remain on China's entity-specific dual-use control list (added 22 Jun). The broad October-2025 MOFCOM export controls stay SUSPENDED only until 10 Nov 2026 (~3 months out). Lynas has advanced ex-China heavy-REE production and DoD-backed Western supply continues to build.
items.actionable: Structural Western-supply validation for the ex-China rare-earth watchlist (Lynas heavy-REE, MP's DoD backing, UUUU's build-out), but the 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff is the calendar catalyst: near-term pricing urgency stays eased, so accumulate MP/UUUU on weakness into a potential control snap-back rather than chase the strategic re-rate now.

items.headline: Tencent pauses buyback into results blackout ahead of 12 Aug interim earnings
items.summary: Tencent ran near-daily buybacks through early July (e.g. ~1.065M shares/HK$500.7M on 9 Jul) under its 10% AGM mandate, then PAUSED the program into the customary blackout ahead of its 12 August interim results. Separately, an HKEXnews notice showed Tencent cutting its Kuaishou (1024) stake from ~15.68% to ~9.37%, ceasing to be a substantial shareholder. Xiaomi's own buyback continued (3.9M shares/HK$100.7M, 15 Jul).
items.actionable: The buyback blackout temporarily lifts a mechanical support under Tencent into its 12 Aug print — a reason not to add aggressively before results, even as the internet sleeve stays the preferred HK-tech core over the SMIC chip leg. The Kuaishou trim is capital recycling, not a read on Tencent's own franchise. Watch the 12 Aug earnings (buyback resumes after) as the next catalyst.
